blocks.text: Pliny writes, Hist. Nat. book 10, ch. 42, §. 58, that the psittacus [parrot] is called Sittace in India. Reland, in Dissertatt. Miscellann. vol. 1, p. 184, thinks this name was formed from Tedac, and this from תך: "whether," he says, "from תך others made تدك [tdk] by doubling the first letter or adding a letter of similar sound, or whether תך arose from Tedac by dropping one of the first two letters because of the similarity of sound." How slippery and uncertain this is, everyone will see for himself. I pass over the dreams of others about this word; whoever wishes to know them may consult Simonis, Lexic. under the word. For my part, I would think one should rest content with what Bochart has argued here no less acutely than learnedly.
Pliny, book 11, ch. 38: "On the head peacocks have crests of hairy little tufts like small trees."
